Climate change is altering species distributions globally, with potentially important consequences for predator communities and ecosystem functioning. Raptors may be particularly informative indicators of these changes, yet projections of future suitability remain uncertain. Here, I used maximum entropy species distribution models (MaxEnt) to quantify current and future environmental suitability for 16 breeding raptor species across the United Kingdom (UK), with future suitability projected under five global climate models (GCMs), two emissions scenarios (SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5), and two time periods (2041–2060 and 2061–2080). Spatially cross-validated model performance varied among species (mean AUC = 0.607–0.848; TSS = 0.077–0.563), with 13 of 16 species having mean TSS scores < 0.40. Chondrichthyans (sharks, skates, rays and chimaeras) are among the most threatened marine vertebrates, yet their conservation in the North‐East Atlantic remains poorly addressed. Marine protected areas (MPAs) constitute key spatial conservation tools but their contribution to chondrichthyan conservation has not been systematically evaluated. Forty‐one chondrichthyan species (18 continental shelf and 23 deep‐water), predominantly demersal, had sufficient occurrence data to model their distribution across the North‐East Atlantic. Overgrazing of macrophytes is an increasing ecological threat to coastal ecosystems, that occurs due to overfishing of top predators and/or to rapid tropicalization of temperate systems. Tropicalization is driven mostly by range expansion or bioinvasion of tropical species assisted by ocean warming. The Mediterranean Sea is a global hotspot of tropicalization where tropical rabbitfish are already a major threat to marine forests in the eastern basin, turning forests into turf barrens. Recently, the expanding invasion of the sea urchin Diadema setosum may further increase this threat to Mediterranean reef ecosystems. In 2006, this invader coming from the Indo Pacific, the Persian Gulf and the Red Sea, was discovered on the coasts of Turkey, and its populations have since expanded to both the eastern and southeastern Mediterranean. item.title: Explaining an early ground-nesting bee emergence with climate and occurrence data: Temperature, not precipitation, advances onset
item.description:
相关度 55.0 · 用百年发生记录解释蜜蜂物候提前，涉及occurrence数据但非分布建模

Understanding the drivers of bee phenology is important for predicting how climate change may alter the temporal overlap between bee activity and plant flowering, with consequences for pollination. We documented unusually early emergence of Melissodes tepidus timberlakei Cockerell, 1926 at a perennial nesting site in spring 2026 and examined the relationship between emergence and climatic conditions with (1) five years of nesting observations at a single site, and (2) 119 years of M. tepidus occurrence records from across the western United States. We found that warming temperatures were associated with earlier emergence, whereas precipitation was not, and we emphasize the utility of monitoring ground nests to understand emergence drivers in bees during ongoing climate change.

Effective wildlife monitoring is essential for biodiversity conservation and sustainable management, particularly in the face of rapid environmental changes and human–wildlife interactions. Advances in camera trap technology and citizen science, that is, nonprofessional involvement in scientific research, provide noninvasive methods for tracking species distribution, abundance, and behavior across large spatial and temporal scales. To address these issues, we introduce Trapper Citizen Science (Trapper CS), an open‐source platform combining artificial intelligence–based data processing pipelines with citizen science to enhance wildlife monitoring efforts. item.description:

Biological invasions are costly economically and environmentally. Despite international agreements to mitigate invasions, we have limited understanding of recent trends - the last two decades of invasion records have been typically excluded from analyses, given potential discovery and reporting lags. We use simulations to show discovery lags do not cause spurious recent declines, but reporting lags can do so. Using global empirical patterns, we estimated reporting lags caused up to a 94% underestimation of recent invasion rates. After controlling for these lags, our model estimated that the invasion rate accelerated at 1.5%/yr between 1970 and 2003 up to a maximum of ~650 species/yr, but has since declined to ~150 species/yr in 2020. The vulnerability of habitats to plant invasions varies widely, yet habitat identity is often overlooked in large‐scale studies of alien species naturalization. Using the newly developed SynHab database, which links 7250 alien vascular plant species to 14 habitat types across 102 regions worldwide, we assessed the role of different habitats in determining the distribution of naturalized alien plants. We identified which habitats are most vulnerable to invasions by naturalized plants, and how climate, environmental conditions, and human impacts interact with habitat type to determine naturalization levels in world regions. When aggregated into six broad categories, human‐made habitats had the highest number of naturalized species (n = 5483), followed by woody habitats (n = 3463), grasslands (n = 2741), stressful habitats (n = 2741), wetlands (n = 2585), and aquatic habitats (n = 190). We evaluate an iterative Bayesian forecast model of black‐legged tick ( Ixodes scapularis ) phenology and population dynamics at near‐term to interannual (e.g., 12‐month) scales. Effective management of recovering large carnivores depends on monitoring systems that are accurate, scalable, and cost‐efficient. This need is particularly acute in Europe, where rapid wolf recolonization is creating new challenges for management and policy. Individual identification, on which conventional monitoring often relies, can be costly and logistically demanding, but for social carnivores the reproductive unit can be a more practical and management‐relevant target. Building on this, we conducted systematic winter camera trap surveys between 2015 and 2023 at 102 fixed sites in the Western Swiss Alps and characterized gray wolf recolonization dynamics without individual identifications. Illegal killing for ivory is the primary threat to the endangered African savanna elephant (Loxodonta africana). Botswana has the world's largest elephant population and experienced little poaching during the continent-wide poaching outbreak of the early 2000's. In 2018, however, evidence of widespread elephant poaching in Botswana began to appear, with an estimated 385 elephants poached. Here, we update the status of elephant poaching in northern Botswana with new data collected in 2023-2026. We also used spatial models to determine the factors associated with elephant poaching locations and to better understand poacher behavior. From late 2023 through mid-2026, we located 202 poached elephants in a ~10,000 km2 area of northern Botswana, north and east of the Okavango Delta and mostly west of Chobe National Park. item.title: Migration strategy and colonization: the disproportionate role of partial migration
item.description:
相关度 72.0 · 提出部分迁徙者更易定殖新区域，可解释分布与预测全球变化下的定殖物种

Colonization drives diversification and determines how species shift their ranges, making it central to ecology and evolution. As both seasonal migration and dispersal depend on locomotor capacity, migration could be a major yet overlooked route to colonization. Here, we present evidence that partially migratory species are disproportionately successful in founding new populations, whereas strict migrants establish more rarely despite routinely reaching potentially suitable habitat in novel areas. Building on the threshold model of migration, we propose that partial migrants’ liability to migrate lies closer to the threshold and/or is more environmentally sensitive, allowing displaced individuals to settle. This mechanism can help explain species distributions and diversification and predict which species might colonize newly suitable areas under global environmental change.
